title: Cycle detection: subtract only pure-mod edges, not any pair carrying a mod declaration
description: Follow-up from review of sutra/304. `module_declaration_edges()` (src/db/graph.rs) selects DISTINCT (file_id, resolved_file_id) pairs where kind='mod'. Cycle detection subtracts these pairs from the edge set before re-running SCC (src/constraints/check.rs:543-544). The subtraction is PAIR-granular, not edge-kind-granular: when a parent both declares a child (`mod child;`) AND substantively imports it (`use child::Foo;`), both rows resolve to the same (parent, child) pair, DISTINCT collapses them, and the pair is dropped — even though a genuine `use` edge independently exists. This suppresses a real parent<->child mutual-use 2-cycle, contradicting the docstring's claim that the loop "exists *only* because of the mod edge". Larger SCCs are protected by the SCC re-run; the false-negative window is parent-child 2-cycles. Existing tests only exercise disjoint file pairs.

acceptance_criteria.text: module_declaration_edges() drops only pairs held together PURELY by module declarations (a mod pair with no non-mod import row for the same file pair)
A parent<->child cycle where the parent has both `mod child;` and `use child::X` (and child uses super) is REPORTED
A pure `mod child;` + `use super::X` re-export cycle stays suppressed (sutra/304 behavior preserved)
New test covers the overlapping-pair case (same pair carrying both mod and use rows)

execution_record: Refined the SQL with a NOT EXISTS subquery so a mod pair is subtracted only when no non-mod import row exists for the same (file_id, resolved_file_id). Added test parent_child_cycle_with_real_use_edge_still_fires (parent has both mod + use to child, child uses super) asserting exactly one cycle fires. Full constraints-test suite: 61 passed. Clippy clean on touched lines (remaining warnings are pre-existing in unrelated files). Went as planned.
root_cause: module_declaration_edges() subtracted file pairs at (file_id, resolved_file_id) granularity keyed only on kind='mod'. A parent that both `mod child;` and `use child::X;` yields two import rows collapsing to one pair; the pair matched the mod query and was dropped wholesale, discarding the co-located genuine `use` edge and suppressing the real parent<->child cycle.
